config.title: Bike Lights in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: When Berlin evenings actually go dark, what German law asks for, which lights are approved, what a police stop costs, and which routes close with the light.

items.q: When do I legally have to switch my bike lights on in Berlin?
items.a: From twilight, not from full darkness. StVO §17 requires lighting bei Dämmerung, bei Dunkelheit oder wenn die Sichtverhältnisse es sonst erfordern, so the obligation starts the moment the sun is down and also applies in heavy rain or fog in the middle of the afternoon. In Berlin in late September that twilight window lasts about 34 minutes after sunset, and by December it is closer to 42 minutes because the sun drops at a shallower angle.

items.q: When does a normal Berlin evening commute go dark?
items.a: It depends on the hour you ride. An 18:30 ride home starts after sunset from 8 October and after the last twilight from 24 October, which is around 170 evenings until the daylight returns at the end of March. Sunset in Berlin falls from 19:55 on 1 September to 18:47 on 30 September, and then the clocks go back on 25 October and remove another hour in a single night.

items.q: Are battery bike lights legal in Germany?
items.a: Yes. StVZO §67 allows a dynamo, a battery or a rechargeable pack on any bicycle, and that has been true since 2017. The older rule that only racing bikes could skip the dynamo no longer applies. What matters is the approval mark rather than the power source.

items.q: What is the K number on a bike light?
items.a: It is the German type approval mark: a wavy line, the letter K and a number issued by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, usually stamped on the underside of the housing near the mount. A light without it is not approved for road use here, however bright it is, and plenty of lights sold online have no K number at all. Check for the stamp before you buy.

items.q: Can I use a flashing bike light in Berlin?
items.a: Not on the bicycle itself. Flashing front and rear lights are prohibited under StVZO §67, with one exception for a rear light that has an emergency-braking function. A blinking light clipped to a bag or a helmet is allowed as an addition but never as a replacement for the fixed set. Proper turn indicators are a separate case and became legal for bicycles and pedelecs in June 2024.

items.q: What else does the law require beyond the two lights?
items.a: A white forward-facing reflector, a red non-triangular rear reflector of class Z which is often built into the tail light, yellow pedal reflectors facing forward and back, and side visibility from either continuous reflective strips on the tyres or rims, fully reflective spokes, or two yellow spoke reflectors set opposite each other on each wheel. Reflective stickers on the frame are not an approved substitute.

items.q: What is the fine for riding without lights in Berlin?
items.a: Twenty euro if the lighting is missing or not working during twilight, darkness or poor visibility. Twenty-five euro if you endangered other traffic at the same time, and thirty-five euro if it contributed to an accident or damage. There are no points for a normal bicycle. Lights that are fitted but switched off, dirty or covered count the same as missing ones.

items.q: Do bike lights actually reduce the risk in Berlin?
items.a: The strongest argument is in the cause breakdown rather than the fine. Berlin police recorded 1,463 turning errors by other road users against cyclists in 2025, against 512 for the cyclists' own most frequent error. A turning driver has about a second to register you, and the only thing facing them is your front light. The clearest seasonal signal in the statistics is on the pedestrian side: 227 accidents in November 2024 and 236 in December 2024 against a 2024 monthly average of 185.

items.q: Which Berlin junctions see the most cyclist accidents?
items.a: In 2025 the five most frequent locations were Schönhauser Allee with 27, Warschauer Straße with 23, and then Chausseestraße, Sonnenallee and Karl-Marx-Straße with 22 each. Those are also the kind of places the police visibility campaign works in October, when about 260 actions run across the city.

items.q: When does Tempelhofer Feld close in autumn and winter?
items.a: The gates follow the sun and change on the first of each month: 06:00 to 21:30 in September, 07:00 to 19:00 in October, 07:00 to 18:00 in November and 07:30 to 17:00 in December and January. The step from 30 September to 1 October removes two and a half hours overnight. You can still leave through the turnstiles at the main entrances after closing, but you cannot get in, so a commute that crosses the Feld has to go round it from 1 October.
